articles.title: Cs White Blue
articles.summary: Cool blue-grey fine woven sparkle, even and calm, satin metal with a faint grid texture. Reads as a vivid teal and purple marbled swirl, busy and watery, with the bands blurring into a shifting two-tone shimmer.
articles.what: Up close: Dense contour-line moire: wavy bands about 8 to 12 px wide in teal and violet, flowing in parallel sweeps at the upper left and breaking into twisty loops, whorls and eddies toward the centre, like fingerprints or water interference. A third blue-indigo shade shows in the gaps. From a distance: Reads as a vivid teal and purple marbled swirl, busy and watery, with the bands blurring into a shifting two-tone shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 129, roughness 70, coat 126. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, stock car, open wheel.
how: This finish is not listed in the Base Material picker, so you cannot pick it there.
Open the AI copilot (the ✦ AI button, bottom right) and ask for it by name, for example "put Cs White Blue on the hood".
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: wide panels show the flow and whorls
Whole body for the full marble effect; keep numbers on a plate
Very busy: numbers need a solid plate with a thick outline; small numbers vanish in the contours.
Nothing busy: the ripples are already the design
Pairs well with: white, chrome, orange, black.
Not listed in the picker: ask the AI copilot for it by name.
pitfalls: Not a smooth gradient: it is fine contour bands, so it looks busy
Not carbon or weave: no regular grid, the lines flow organically
Avoid: muddying with more grey, tiny thin pinstripes that vanish.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 129 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 70 (satin gloss), clearcoat 126 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: muddying with more grey, tiny thin pinstripes that vanish.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: nothing busy: the ripples are already the design; a solid plate for numbers and logos: the contours cut through small text
Patterns to avoid: stripes, camo, grids or weave: moire against the bands; other loud colour-shift or glitter patterns: stack too much
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat for a deep wet look; fine sparkle only if wanted, it already has plenty
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
